doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Train to New York via Philadelphia and Atlantic City
summary: At twenty, he travels with fifty dollars, stops at Knoxville, and searches for Danny Ryan and bandleaders.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That’s when I took the train. I had fifty dollars in my pocket. I stopped at Knoxville, Tennessee to see the Pelicans, New Orleans Pelicans, play a double header. Don’t ask me where I put my horns, where I checked them, and the conductor says, “Yeah son, you can get off and take the next train.” I did this all myself. I was just 20 years old.
And did have you have a specific destination?

Yeah. New York. But I had to stop in Philadelphia first, because Danny Ryan, who was a trumpet player that I played with in a nightclub, he wanted me to go to New York with him. I says, “Danny, I’m not ready yet.” But then when finally the theater closed, the Orpheum Theater closed, that’s when I headed for New York, but I stopped in Philadelphia. I stopped in Philadelphia, this is good. I stopped at the rooming house and the lady came out, she says, “Oh Danny is not here, he is playing in Ocean City with Ray” (something band). I went to Ocean City and he was there and he says, “Al you remember Adrian Fleist, the cellist?” I said yes. He said, “He’s playing with George Olsen.” George Olsen was a big name at this time.
